best_for: Windows users who take many screenshots a day for support tickets, docs or chats and want capture, markup and upload done in one keystroke.
description:
ShareX is a screenshot, screen recording and file sharing tool made by the ShareX Team. The team says it has been in active development for more than 18 years, and its interface comes in close to 30 languages.

Before you save or send a shot, you can mark it up with arrows, boxes, text, speech balloons and numbered steps, and blur or pixelate anything private. The image editor also crops, cuts out parts and can remove the background. Uploads are not just for images: you can send a folder, text, the clipboard or a URL, or let ShareX watch a folder and upload whatever lands in it. If you liked the older look, ShareX Classic keeps the version 21 interface.

points.title: Capture any way you like
points.text: Full screen, a window, a monitor or a region, plus scrolling capture, screen recording and GIF recording. Since 22.0 it records the screen natively, without FFmpeg.

points.title: Actions after the shot
points.text: Each capture can run a chain of tasks: open the editor, add effects, copy, save, pin to screen, run OCR, upload, shorten the link or show a QR code.

points.title: Uploads go where you choose
points.text: ShareX uploads only to services you set up, and supports custom uploaders. The privacy policy says the app itself collects no data.

points.title: Free, no ads
points.text: It is open source under the GPL, costs nothing and shows no ads. Version 22.4.0 came out in November 2026.

points.title: About 37 extra tools
points.text: Beyond capture it bundles tools for color, images, video, text and system tasks. It checks GitHub for updates at startup and from time to time, and installs one only when you agree.

points.title: Windows only for now
points.text: macOS and Linux builds exist only as previews that need a GitHub sign-in to download and expire after 90 days. The project dropped Windows 7 in version 18.0.

points.title: Install options
points.text: This page lists 64-bit installers for one user or all users and keeps 24 versions. A portable build, the Microsoft Store and Steam are other options.
